chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who forgets the Takbirat al-Iftitah (the opening Takbir), he said: 'He must repeat (the prayer).'

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةَ الِافْتِتَاحِ: The opening Takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') at the beginning of prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the opening Takbir during prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes that forgetting the opening Takbir necessitates a full repetition of the prayer, highlighting its status as a fundamental pillar of validity in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the scholarly consensus on the necessity of conscious intention and verbal declaration at the onset of prayer, distinguishing it from minor omissions that may be rectified by prostration of forgetfulness (Sujud al-Sahw).
